jobs.title: Clif Bar Warehouse Team Member (Night Shift 600pm - 600am)
jobs.description:
## Join Us in Leading the Future of Snacking

Are you ready to Make It Happen at Mondelēz International? We’re the team behind iconic brands like Oreo, Ritz, and Chips Ahoy!, and we’re looking for a motivated Warehouse Team Member to join our Indianapolis plant on the night shift.

### What You’ll Do

You’ll play a hands-on role in our warehouse operations, ensuring materials move safely and efficiently from receiving to production to shipping. Your days will be varied and fast-paced. You'll operate stand-up counterbalance forklifts, reach trucks, and powered pallet jacks, and use SAP-EWM or RF systems to manage everything from put-away to replenishment. Supporting the Vongal palletizer and inline wrapper operations will also be part of your routine — you’ll keep material flowing and address minor jams, escalating bigger issues to maintenance.

You’ll also:
- Replenish raw and packaging materials into production areas and dough room kits
- Handle trailer loading and unloading, following strict dock safety controls (wheel chocks, gladhand locks, dock lights)
- Use the pallet inverter to transfer materials between wood, plastic, or CHEP pallets
- Complete all SAP transactions accurately for goods movements, confirming lot codes and quantities

### What Safety & Quality Look Like Here

Safety isn’t just a poster on the wall — it’s how we work. You’ll wear required PPE (safety shoes, hearing protection, high-visibility vest), perform daily pre-use inspections on powered equipment, and tag out any machine that needs service. Every near miss or unsafe condition is reported immediately. Food safety is also critical: you’ll inspect materials for damage or contamination, maintain allergen control, and ensure proper segregation of Good/Hold/Reject items.

### Systems & Inventory Accuracy

You’ll keep our inventory visible and accurate in real time by executing warehouse transactions in SAP-EWM/ECC. Cycle counts, wall-to-wall inventories, and reconciling physical vs. system counts will be part of your routine. If you spot a discrepancy, you’ll escalate it promptly to inventory control or supervision.

### Continuous Improvement & Teamwork

We believe in always getting better. You’ll take part in IL6S, Kaizen, and 5S initiatives that improve safety, quality, and efficiency. You’ll keep your workspace clean, organized, and audit-ready, and you’ll communicate regularly with Production, Quality, Maintenance, Planning, and Logistics teams. If you have experience to share, you’ll help train new team members by modeling safe, standardized work practices.

### What You’ll Need

**Required:**
- High school diploma or GED
- At least 3 years experience in a warehouse, distribution, or manufacturing environment
- 2+ years operating Powered Industrial Vehicles (PIV), including stand-up counterbalance and stand-up reach forklifts
- Familiarity with SAP-EWM or other WMS, plus RFID use
- Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and work in a food-grade environment
- Strong adaptability to take on diverse responsibilities

**Preferred:**
- Experience with automated palletizing or packaging equipment (Vongal, inline wrappers)
- Prior work in food manufacturing, 3PL, or consumer goods
- Knowledge of IL6S, Lean, or 5S principles

### Work Environment & Schedule

This is a warehouse and production floor setting with variable temperatures, exposed to forklifts, conveyors, palletizers, and moderate noise levels. The night shift runs 6:00pm to 6:00am on a 2-2-3 schedule — you’ll work two days, have two off, then work three, repeating the pattern.

### Compensation & Benefits

The hourly wage for this position is **$23.09/hr**. You’ll also be eligible for an annual incentive program targeting 5% of your salary. Mondelez International offers a comprehensive benefits package including health insurance, wellness programs, family support resources, life and disability insurance, a 401K retirement savings plan, paid leave, education-related programs, paid holidays and vacation time — many of which are subsidized or fully paid by the company.

Mondelez Global LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We welcome all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

Weekly paychecks and contractual annual wage progression raises complete a benefits offering that no comparable part-time warehouse job with benefits in this market can match.

jobs.title: East Chicago Night Shift Sortation Warehouse Associate with $20-$23/hr
jobs.description:
Role Based in East Chicago

Key Information

  • Employer: Amazon (Hiring in East Chicago)
  • Worksite: East Chicago, IN
  • Position: Night Shift Sortation Warehouse Associate (Based in East Chicago)
  • This East Chicago-based role is an excellent opportunity for professionals skilled in relevant skills.
  • Our Amazon team in East Chicago, IN is growing.
  • Benefit from working in East Chicago, a key hub for the Logistics industry.

Salary and Benefits

  • Pay: $20-$23/Hour (approx. $26.3k/Year)
  • Benefits: A comprehensive benefits package is included.
  • Stable workload with modern tooling and processes.

What You'll Do

  • This role centers on your professional skills within the Logistics space in East Chicago.

Mastering the Overnight Middle Mile

If the fulfillment center is the brain of the operation, the sortation center is the central nervous system. Welcome to the critical "middle mile" of the Amazon delivery network. As a Night Shift Sortation Warehouse Associate, your primary objective is to group and route thousands of packages during the graveyard hours so they reach the correct local delivery hubs right at dawn. For those seeking highly active, fast-paced night shift warehouse jobs that offer intense teamwork and rapid physical movement, this is the ultimate environment.

The Overnight Sortation Experience

Work in a sort center is fundamentally different from a traditional fulfillment role. You are not picking individual items; you are dealing with sealed, completed packages that are moving rapidly down vast networks of conveyor belts. The atmosphere at night is charged, highly focused, and incredibly team-oriented. When the conveyor belts get heavily loaded during the midnight "rush," you will rely on your night-owl teammates to clear the lines and keep the supply chain moving seamlessly.

  1. Rapid Package Routing: You will read complex digital routing labels as packages fly down the line, pulling them off the belt and sorting them into specific geographical chutes or designated postal carts.
  2. Pallet Architecture: You will become a master of spatial reasoning. Sorting requires building perfectly stable, tightly packed pallets of boxes (often referred to as "playing Tetris" by our veteran associates), which are then heavily shrink-wrapped to prevent transit damage.
  3. Fluid Loading Operations: Utilizing manual pallet jacks, you will safely transport these massive, wrapped pallets directly into the bellies of outbound 18-wheeler semi-trailers, staging them for the early morning over-the-road drivers.

"The night sort center moves incredibly fast, but the overnight shift premium is what keeps me here. Working the graveyard shift allows me to manage my college classes during the day while still getting access to Amazon's incredible 401(k) matching and tuition assistance. The night crew is like a family." - A current Night Sortation Associate.

Flexibility and Night Shift Rewards

We understand that modern life requires flexible schedules. Sortation roles offer some of the most adaptable late-night shifts in the logistics careers landscape, including midnight to morning or late evening options. Associates unlock exceptional health, dental, and vision benefits, along with highly competitive shift differentials that significantly boost your base pay when working non-traditional hours. You will need a strong commitment to workplace safety, the ability to lift up to 49 pounds, and a High School diploma or equivalent to join the night team.

jobs.description:
Position Warehouse Associate
Location Chicago Heights, IL
Company UPS
Pay Rate $25.50/hr
Job Type Part-Time
Urgency
Highlights Weekly Pay

Chicago Heights Alert: We are currently seeking a Warehouse Associate to join our local team. This is an excellent opportunity for anyone looking for part-time work with $25.50/hr potential.

Tags: #ChicagoHeightsJobs #PartTime #Warehouse



About UPS & Our Culture

Full-time employment at UPS is one of the most sought-after positions in American blue-collar work — and for good reason. Our Full-Time Warehouse Associates are Teamsters union members earning contractually guaranteed wages, working inside one of the most technologically advanced distribution center networks on earth. When you search for full-time warehouse jobs that offer weekly pay, comprehensive benefits, and a genuine long-term career path, the UPS full-time warehouse associate role consistently sits at the top of every honest comparison. We build careers here — not just shifts — and the associates who commit to UPS full-time consistently build lives their peers envy.

What Our Team Says (Employee Reviews)

"Going full-time at UPS was the single best career decision I have ever made. The Teamsters contract gives me wages, benefits, and job security that my friends in other industries genuinely cannot believe. My medical coverage is better than what most white-collar professionals receive, my pension is real and growing, and I have a clear path to a driver salary that will set my family up for decades. This is what a full-time warehouse job is supposed to look like." - Current Full-Time Warehouse Associate, Chicago, IL.

Role Overview & Responsibilities

As a UPS Full-Time Warehouse Associate, you work a structured daily shift inside our package center, operating across the full range of warehouse functions — loading, unloading, sorting, and staging — with the stability of a permanent schedule, guaranteed weekly hours, and a Teamsters contract behind every paycheck.

  • Full-Shift Sort Operations: Execute the complete daily sort cycle — inbound unloading, package sorting, and outbound loading — across an 8-hour structured shift with dedicated break periods, consistent start times, and a predictable weekly schedule you can plan your life around.
  • Cross-Function Expertise: Develop mastery across multiple warehouse functions over time, becoming a versatile full-time associate capable of leading in any area of the sort operation where the shift manager needs experienced coverage.
  • Mentorship of Part-Time Associates: As an experienced full-time presence, model UPS safety methods and load quality standards for newer part-time team members, helping the facility's overall accuracy and safety performance rise every shift.

Benefits & Perks

Full-Time Warehouse Associates receive the complete Teamsters union benefit package — medical, dental, and vision insurance, a defined-benefit pension plan, paid vacation, paid sick leave, and paid holidays. Weekly direct-deposit paychecks, annual contractual wage progression raises, and priority consideration for full-time driver openings make this one of the most financially rewarding full-time warehouse jobs available in any market.

jobs.title: Vice President, Solution Sales - Distribution & Fulfillment (P/LS)
jobs.description:
ITS Logistics is a leading Third-Party Logistics provider and an Echo Global Logistics company. We run a fully integrated platform - asset-based truckload, Dedicated & Fulfillment, LTL, Dray, Intermodal, and Managed Transportation - plus Roadtex, our temperature-controlled warehouse and distribution network. That combination gives our customers something most 3PLs can't offer: a single partner who can handle ambient fulfillment, confectionery-grade temp-controlled distribution, and everything in between.

We're a performance-driven organization. We invest in our people, give them real commercial infrastructure to work with, and get out of their way. If you're looking for a place where your output actually matters, this is it.

Want to learn more about ITS Logistics? Check out our website! www.its4logistics.com

About the Position

We're looking for a proven hunter who has spent their career selling warehouse and fulfillment solutions into the pharmaceutical and life sciences space - and who understands that in this vertical, compliance capability is the sale, not a checkbox.

This role sells the full ITS + Roadtex D&F platform: ITS omnichannel ambient warehouse and fulfillment for CPG manufacturers, food shippers, and e-commerce customers, and Roadtex temperature-controlled (confectionery-grade, 55–65°F) warehouse, distribution, and value-added services for customers who need food-safe, OTIF-compliant, retail-ready distribution.

There is no existing book to manage. You will prospect, qualify, design solutions, and close - from first call through contract. The platform is differentiated. The opportunity is real. We need someone who can execute.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prospect and close new business within the pharma and life sciences vertical - targeting pharmaceutical manufacturers, specialty distributors, clinical logistics providers, medical device companies, and nutraceutical brands.
  • Sell the full ITS + Roadtex D&F platform: ambient omnichannel fulfillment (ITS) and confectionery-grade temperature-controlled warehouse, distribution, and VAS (Roadtex).
  • Build and manage your own pipeline from scratch. Qualify opportunities, design integrated solutions, coordinate pricing, and lead pursuit cycles through close.
  • Engage VP and C-suite supply chain, logistics, and procurement contacts. This is not a coordinator-level sales motion.
  • Build multi-service proposals and ROI models - combining ambient warehouse, temp-controlled storage, VAS, and transportation into a single integrated solution.
  • Work with ITS and Roadtex operations and pricing teams to validate solutions operationally before proposals go out.
  • Use the Echo enterprise account base to identify cross-sell opportunities for ITS D&F and Roadtex capabilities.
  • Keep CRM clean - accurate deal values, stages, timelines, and probabilities on every active opportunity.
  • Transition closed accounts cleanly to the Enterprise Account Management team and stay involved where needed to protect revenue actualization.
  • Show up at trade events, customer meetings, and industry forums specific to food and nutrition supply chain.
  • Give leadership straight pipeline reporting - what's real, what's at risk, what's closing.

A bout the Requirements

  • 7+ years as an individual contributor selling 3PL warehouse and fulfillment solutions. Not sales management - field sales, closing deals.
  • You've consistently closed $12M+ per year in new logo warehouse and fulfillment revenue within the food, beverage, or nutrition space. We'll ask for specifics.
  • You built that pipeline yourself. Not from marketing programs, not from account lists handed to you. You know how to generate your own opportunities.
  • You are actively hunting in your current role - not managing accounts, not renewing contracts. You find new business and close it.
  • The product you've been selling is warehouse and fulfillment - physical 3PL services. Not transportation brokerage, not TMS, not managed services.
  • You understand how shippers evaluate 3PL outsourcing decisions - the RFP process, the stakeholders involved, how multi-year contracts get structured and won.
  • You've sold into food, beverage, nutrition, or CPG verticals and understand the compliance environment: OTIF, MABD, retail routing guide requirements.
  • You can engage confidently at VP and C-suite level and lead a complex, multi-stakeholder sales process without hand-holding.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, or a related field.

Work environment/physical demands summary:

This job operates in an office environment and uses a computer, telephone and other office equipment as needed to perform duties. The noise level in the work environment is typical of that of an office with an open seating floor plan. The employee may encounter frequent interruptions throughout the work day. The employee is regularly required to sit, talk, or hear.

jobs.title: Warehouse Associate - 2nd Shift - Days Off: Tuesdays & Wednesdays
jobs.description:
Warehouse Associate - 2nd Shift

Warehouse associates will ensure the needs of both production and warehouse are met throughout their respective shifts by the timely and safe delivery, shipping, and receiving of produce and packaged goods.

Detailed Responsibilities

Receiving

  • Will apply glad hand lock and wheel chocks for any trailer to unload
  • Will assist FSQA and receivers with breakdown of pallets for quality checks and to transport to storage
  • When produce or packaged good are received in the associate will place produce/packaged goods into correct storage
  • Placed produce/packaging must be staged according to FIFO and in correct temperature storage location and remove any plastic from produce that needs to breathe
  • Notify leadership if any product is found to be out of correct location
  • Work on creating space for inbound loads
  • Ensure all storage pods are kept free of debris

Replenishing

  • Set floor for decanting and shipping lines per drop list and boxing call out
  • All packaging material is set for box team, shipping lines, and decanting area
  • Prior to production running completely out of product, the warehouse associate will bring out the requested material according to the production's count.
  • Answer call of any additional product needs for production
  • Move anything needed for production, warehouse, sanitation, or FSQA
  • Prior to leaving for any break, warehouse associates will check with the production team as well as make a visual check of produce/packaging in use to ensure the area is fully stocked before leaving production area.
  • Near the end of each shift remove any material from the drop zone as well as the return area that production will not use for the incoming shift. All product is returned to home location
  • Ensure all pallets in storage are front faced, leveled, and plastic removed
  • Warehouse associate is responsible for organization of assigned storage areas

Shipping

  • Check all trailers loaded on the shipping dock for trash or pine pallets, remove any items found that are not needed for completed shipments
  • Put on glad hand lock on trailer and chock wheels prior to being loaded
  • Using the load diagram form load trucks with completed pallets with management approval - full load 26 pallets
  • Once the trailer has been fully loaded, place a FedEx seal on the closed trailer door to signify ready for ship and put the serial number for the load seal on the load diagram form and we remove the glad hand lock. Turn in paperwork to leadership

Support other Warehouse functions

  • We are one team. Team members are expected to assist with completing any function needed for our company to deliver finished goods to the customer. This includes using any equipment certified on or assisting other departments to get the job done for the day.

General Responsibilities

  • Follow all safety procedures throughout execution of all tasks. This includes, but is not limited to, performing pre-shift equipment checks for all equipment used and wearing required PPE. Safety first!
  • Follow the facility GMPs and help enforce them throughout the facility.
  • Sign for all equipment needed to perform your duties. Ensure these are signed back in upon completion of shift.
  • Support the efforts of the company to maintain our food safety system (SQF) and quality programs. Quality always!
  • Be respectful of others. Team members are expected to carry themselves in a professional manner in all situations and at all times.

Qualifications

  • General high school degree, or equivalent, (e.g. GED). GED or High School diploma required
  • Willing to learn how to operate equipment needed to perform all warehouse duties including, but not limited to, manual and electric pallet jack and hand held scanners.
  • Able to lift up to 50lbs
  • Previous warehouse experience preferred

jobs.description:
Job Description:

The 2023 US Best Managed Company Award recognizes companies that outperform their competition in the four critical areas of management: strategic planning, effective execution, culture, and governance/financial performance. As a recipient of this accolade, Coke Florida has distinguished itself as a leader among U.S. private organizations.

What We Offer:

If you are a full-time employee at Coke Florida, you are eligible to enroll in our Total Rewards Program and take advantage of its many offerings:

  • The all-inclusive plans for wellness consist of medical, dental, and vision coverage that aims to provide complete health support to the employees
  • The employer-sponsored 401K plan includes a healthy company match, ensuring employees receive even higher returns on their contributions
  • Supplemental Life Insurance
  • The company provides its employees with 11 paid holidays and a vacation pay for three weeks annually
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • EAPs may offer a variety of services, including counseling, legal and financial advice, substance abuse treatment, and referrals to community resources
  • Competitive compensation

The Winter Haven Coke Florida site necessitates a Warehouse Lead, and we are hiring for the first shift.

What you will do:

The primary responsibility of a Coke Florida Warehouse Supervisor is to oversee the storage and shipping of materials.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Assumes responsibility for a group of 25-30 warehouse workers
  • Developing a team requires coaching, guiding, collaborating, and enhancing the abilities of those who work together
  • Administer the regular functions of the storage establishment
  • Arrange Warehouse Team Members to Meet Demands of Facility
  • Dedicate a section of your storage area for the proper rotation of goods
  • Assist with the regulation of inventory levels and mitigate the likelihood of product loss
  • Oversee the handling and storage of goods during transportation and upon arrival
  • Secure company assets
  • Adopting cost-cutting measures can help organizations manage labor and OPEX budgets effectively

Attention to detail is essential, as you will be dealing with important information and sensitive client data:

  • The minimum educational requirement for this position is either a high school diploma or its equivalent, the GED
  • This role requires a minimum of two years' relevant experience in the warehouse or distribution field
  • Experience in managing both human and financial resources is a must-have for this position
  • Employers require candidates to possess leadership skills and have at least two years' experience in a warehouse or distribution supervisor role
  • The skill to manage a manual or powered pallet jack proficiently is a fundamental necessity for all individuals responsible for transporting goods
  • You must have forklift certification before starting your job

Having a broad range of skills, knowledge, and experience can make you an invaluable addition to the team. Expanding your expertise in different areas, such as marketing, data analysis, or project management, can show that you are adaptable, flexible, and capable of handling various tasks and projects:

  • Advanced Excel experience
  • Familiarity with the efficient management of inventory systems and aptitude with SAP software preferred

The role requires a significant amount of physical effort, which means:

  • The talent to repeatedly raise, carry, and position bulky objects weighing up to 50 pounds without any help is mandatory
  • The position demands that the individual has the strength to push and pull items weighing no more than 50 pounds. The tasks should be executed while bending at the knees, kneeling, squatting, and reaching at different levels
  • The competency to use manual transport equipment (e.g. pallet jack or hand truck) to move product loads repeatedly for a distance of at least 100 yards without any assistance
  • The skill to repeatedly take hold of and operate objects that come in various sizes and weights that require deft finger movements and coordination between the hands and eyes
  • The capacity to sustain physical efforts for prolonged periods of time is a vital requirement for individuals who are involved in jobs that necessitate continuous manual labor
  • Flexibility in Reading Small, Medium, and Large Print
  • Demonstrating the ability to stand for a minimum of 8 hours while at work, and potentially extending up to 10 hours
  • The requirement to walk a minimum of 4 hours during the workday
  • Frequently perform tasks within an environment that is hot and humid indoors
  • The aptitude to equip an auditory aid to comprehend directions delivered in the English tongue

Other details:

  • Job Family: Warehouse
  • Job Function: Warehouse
  • Pay Type: Salary

Coke Florida may update this job description at any time and assign further duties and responsibilities as necessary.

The employee's ability to perform the essential job functions to satisfaction is a prerequisite to employment at Coke Florida. The company may offer reasonable accommodations to disabled employees to enable them to perform their job duties, provided it does not cause undue burden.

All applicants and employees are treated with respect, dignity, and consideration irrespective of their background or identity.

jobs.description:
Job Summary

We are seeking a bilingual dedicated and energetic Janitorial Specialist to maintain cleanliness and safety within a busy warehouse environment. In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring the facility remains spotless, sanitized, and well-maintained, supporting a safe and efficient workspace for all team members. Your proactive approach to cleaning, equipment handling, and safety adherence will help uphold our high standards of sanitation and facility upkeep. This position offers an excellent opportunity for individuals with janitorial or custodial experience who thrive in fast-paced settings and take pride in their work.

Duties

  • Perform comprehensive cleaning tasks across the warehouse, including sweeping, mopping, dusting, and trash removal to maintain a tidy environment.
  • Operate various cleaning equipment such as floor buffers, scrubbers, and vacuums to ensure optimal floor care and sanitation.
  • Handle chemical agents safely by following proper chemical handling safety procedures, including mixing, storage, and disposal.
  • Conduct heavy lifting and manual handling of cleaning supplies, equipment, and waste materials while adhering to safe lifting practices.
  • Maintain sanitation standards by disinfecting high-touch surfaces and ensuring compliance with safety protocols at all times.
  • Support facilities maintenance activities such as minor repairs or reporting issues that require specialized attention.
  • Assist with industrial cleaning tasks including the use of specialized tools for large-scale cleaning projects in the warehouse setting.
  • Provide excellent customer service by responding promptly to cleaning requests or concerns from team members or supervisors.

Experience

  • Prior janitorial or custodial experience in a commercial or industrial setting is preferred.
  • Proven ability to operate cleaning equipment such as floor buffers and scrubbers effectively.
  • Knowledge of chemical agent handling safety procedures and sanitation standards.
  • Experience with heavy lifting and manual handling in a warehouse or facilities environment.
  • Familiarity with safety protocol adherence related to custodial work, including proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
  • Background in facilities maintenance or industrial cleaning is advantageous.
  • Strong attention to detail with a commitment to maintaining high cleanliness standards in busy environments.

Join our team as a Janitorial Specialist and play a vital role in creating a safe, clean, and welcoming warehouse environment! Your dedication to quality cleaning practices combined with your safety awareness will ensure our facility remains efficient and compliant while supporting our team’s success.

  • 401(k) matching
  • Dental insurance

  • Paid time off
  • Vision insurance

In this role, you’re one of the most critical people in the operation. Each day you will fill orders utilizing a scanner gun. After scanning, you will manually lift the cases or buckets onto pallets and then use a rider jack to deliver the pallets to the loading department. You will work in a safe, timely, and accurate manner to keep our shipping department running smoothly, keep the drivers on schedule, and allow us to get paint into stores that depend on us.

Here’s what we’re looking for from you:

  • Attend training. You won’t be out on the floor pulling orders until you are fully trained. You’ll begin with lots of safety training and other education.
  • Safety. We have a meeting and do stretches at the beginning of each shift to warm up and get ready to safely lift paint all day. You will be required to wear proper safety equipment, including steel toed shoes at all times. We’re very proud of our safety record and want you to be part of that.
  • Heavy lifting. The orders come to you electronically and you will pull cases or buckets of paint and load them by hand onto pallets. Cases weigh about 40 lbs and buckets are 75 lbs.
  • A clean facility. You may have worked in dusty or grimy warehouses before, but we pride ourselves on how clean our facility is. We appreciate your help keeping it clean.
  • Diploma or GED. A high school diploma or GED is required.

Here’s what we offer you:

The Freight Handler is a mission‐critical contributor to our Operations team, ensuring freight moves through our network with precision, speed, and zero compromise to safety or quality. As our Smart NetworkTM continues to scale nationwide, the reliability of our dock operations directly impacts transit performance, customer satisfaction, and the integrity of our long‐haul model.    This role exists to keep freight flowing efficiently through the Nashville service center—executing high‐accuracy loading, unloading, tagging, and movement of shipments that power our metro‐to‐metro network. jobs.description:
Graham Packaging is a people, planet and values-based company and a leader in sustainable packaging manufacturing. From the kitchen to the laundry room, Graham Packaging is part of your everyday life.

For employees at Graham, our Blue Culture is part of their everyday lives, too. In other words, Blue is how we do things here.

At Graham, we are united by a clear vision. We know our part and help those around us know theirs, encouraging one another to continuously improve. We create a safe, challenging environment to innovate by supporting creative ideas and new ways of thinking. We take the initiative to cultivate our individual growth and help others do the same, while keeping ourselves and one another accountable. And we actively promote cooperation, collaboration, integrity and respect across regions and teams to foster an engaged, diverse and connected workforce.

We value our employees, and a Blue Culture allows for the most rewarding employee experience as part of the Graham family. Blue is how we feel about what we dotogetherto create a better tomorrow. Working at Graham means you lead constructively with clear goals, use diverse thinking to drive excellence, accountability, innovation, as well as demonstrating collaboration, embracing learning, and taking action for continuous improvement and growth.

Graham Packaging Company is looking for a Forklift Operator based in West Chicago (St. Charles) IL.

Opening is9:00 am- 5:00 pm Monday-Friday.

Starting wage is $ 23.45

Forklift Operators perform a combination of product handling and lift truck operating duties to stack, transport, and store work-in-process and finished goods. Supplies production lines with efficient flow of materials – knockdowns and dividers - and moves finished goods to warehouse. Complete line driver reports accurately and legible showing locations and quantities of raw materials used as well as quantities and locations where finished goods were stored. Assist production line employees by relieving them in breaks and lunchtime periods. The primary duties of a Forklift Operator include:

  • Follow all established safety, health, quality GMP and Company policies, procedures and recognized practices.
  • Perform a safety lift truck inspection and battery check and report any equipment malfunctioning or damage to the Warehouse Manager or Shift Supervisor. Change lift truck batteries and add water when necessary; keep record of time batteries are changed. Fill out lift truck status report.
  • Participate in continuous quality improvement projects and other related activities as assigned.
  • Review daily production schedule with Shift Supervisor, brings materials to the production lines when needed to execute schedule and notify supervisor of any materials running low. Removes finished goods from production lines, back to assigned warehouse locations.
  • Provide accurate information of unloaded materials as well as materials used or produced to warehouse personnel.
  • Remove, store, and unitize production scrap bales and informs warehouse personnel when there is enough for a full load. Removes excess corrugated from mezzanine and empties baler as required. Takes full bales of cardboard scrap from baler to assigned location in the warehouse.
  • Maintain accurate records of materials being used and produced, and reports them in appropriate paperwork, back to warehouse personnel.
  • Remove finished goods and other materials in hold to assigned location. Stores finished goods stacked neatly and in proper height. Verifies that all finished goods removed from the production area must have a product code tag.
  • Participate in physical inventory taking.
  • Keep each production line supplied with the proper knock down cases, dividers, pallets and when each pallet is full take that pallet to the warehouse for loading on the trailer; and takes unused cases and dividers back to the warehouse to the proper location.
  • On limited production, may assist in stock-handler duties or load trailers as needed.
  • Bring up hot glue cases to the mezzanine, brings color concentrate to the lines, replaces cold glue tote, removes excess cases from production floor, brings slip sheets to production floor, loads storage racks with gaylords, set up rework, set up units of product on hold for Q.C., relieves stock handlers, loads and unloads corrugated trailers, identifies good corrugated from the bad and isolates it.
  • Follow established forklift procedures and complete required safety and maintenance checklists
  • Follow established procedures for damaged finished goods and raw materials and report them on line driver report.
  • Communicate with supervisor regarding shift totals and machine totals reports and with other lift truck operators regarding any changes or problems that arise, including damaged materials, damaged skids, or low inventories.
  • Complete written documentation as required.
  • Assist in relieving downstream teammates for breaks and lunches.
  • Use forklift to move pallets of finished product to stretch wrap machines to stretch wrap them and to staging area after wrapping, or to specify warehouse location. Completes finished goods report or worksheet.
  • Maintain supplies of corrugated and other packaging supplies at each machine.
  • Visually inspect all completed pallets of product for quality and conformity to the packaging instructions to ensure quality at the source.
  • Limited travel may be required.


Minimum of 1 year forklift experience preferred.

Forklift Operators are required to interact with other managers, employees, vendors, and customers. Therefore, the following skills and proficiencies are also essential requirements of the position:

  • Ability to maintain regular, predictable, and punctual attendance.
  • Computer usage and typing skills are essential.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication, including the ability to effectively communicate with internal and external customers.
  • Must be able to work under pressure and meet deadlines, while maintaining a positive attitude and providing exemplary customer service.
  • Ability to work independently and to carry out assignments to completion within parameters of instructions given, prescribed routines, and standard accepted practices.
  • Communicates effectively: conveys facts and information clearly both verbally and orally.
  • Collaborates well with others: proactively contributes to group objectives; volunteers to help others.

The expected salary range for the position described in this posting is made in accordance with the legal mandates of certain jurisdictions within the United States. The final agreed-upon compensation is based on individual qualifications and experience.
Benefits include medical, dental, vision and basic life insurance. Employees are able to enroll in the companys 401K Employee Saving Plan and may participate in its Employee Wellness Program. Employees will also receive paid time off in accordance with company policy and state law requirements.
Graham Packaging is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, religion, creed, age, national origin, physical or mental disability, gender identity and/or expression, marital status, veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

JOB SUMMARY

Responsible for putting away inbound produce.

Summer is her, come start a new Career with
FreshPoint Chicago.
Starting Pay $23.24/hour

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Receives and puts away all inbound produce.
  • Ensures product is put away in proper rotation (FIFO).
  • Safe operation of powered industrial equipment.
  • Ensures selection slots are properly stocked with the product always keeps pallets free from tape, wrap or wires and remove empty pallets as needed.
  • Responsible for the cleaning and sanitation of the work area.
  • Accounting for the received product.
  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS
Education

  • Prefer High School or GED

Experience
Six (6) months experience in a warehouse.

  • Six (6) months experience of proficiently utilizing a stand-up forklift and riding pallet jack preferred.
  • Basic knowledge of fresh produce preferred.
  • Experience in replenishment, cycling of product, RF (radio frequency) scanners and other returns related functions preferred.

Skills

  • Must have strong reading, writing, and be able to read, write, and speak English fluently.
  • Ability to perform work assignments at an acceptable productivity level.
  • Able to effectively communicate and interact with others in a professional manner.

Physical Demand

  • Stand for extended periods, bend, stoop, reach, push, pull, squat, turn the body, and walk.
  • Lift and move cases (selecting a product and placing on a pallet) ranging in weight up to 75 lbs continuously to and from heights ranging from floor to knee, waist, shoulder, and overhead.
  • Use hands and fingers to peel and stick labels on cases.
  • Handle and feel objects and/or equipment controls; reach with hands and arms.
  • Must have the ability to talk and hear; must be able to hear warning horns on moving machinery and equipment.
  • Specific vision abilities required to perform this job include close and distance vision, depth perception, color vision, peripheral vision, and the ability to adjust focus.
  • Must exhibit a high level of endurance, energy, and strength to successfully perform the position.

Work Environment

  • Must be able to work in confined spaces

Position in Chicago, IL

Fast Facts

  • Apply your your professional skills skills at our Chicago location.
  • Benefits: This role offers competitive pay.
  • Flexible contract/gig opportunity in Chicago.
  • Employer: UPS (Hiring in Chicago)
  • Job Title: Seasonal Peak Warehouse Sorter — Immediate Hire (Gig/Contract)

  • This Chicago-based role is an excellent opportunity for professionals skilled in relevant skills.
  • Our UPS team in Chicago, IL is growing.
  • Benefit from working in Chicago, a key hub for the Package Logistics industry.

About UPS & Our Culture

When UPS says immediate hire, we mean it. During peak season, our package center teams expand by thousands of associates in a matter of weeks, and we have built our onboarding system to get people working — and getting paid — as fast as any warehouse employer in America. If you are searching for seasonal warehouse jobs hiring immediately with a brand name you trust, competitive hourly pay, and a genuine shot at a permanent career, our Peak Warehouse Sorter position is open and ready for you right now. No lengthy application process, no multi-week waiting period — UPS peak hiring is designed for speed because the packages do not wait for anyone.

What Our Team Says (Employee Reviews)

"I applied on a Monday and was working by Thursday. The onboarding process at UPS during peak is extremely fast and well-organized — they know how to bring large numbers of people in quickly without it feeling chaotic. jobs.description:
Position in Chicago, IL

Snapshot

  • Employer: United Parcel Service (UPS) (Hiring in Chicago)
  • Position: UPS Preload Package Handler (Flexible/Contract, Chicago)
  • Location: Chicago, IL
  • This Chicago-based role is an excellent opportunity for professionals skilled in relevant skills.
  • Our United Parcel Service (UPS) team in Chicago, IL is growing.
  • Benefit from working in Chicago, a key hub for the Warehousing And Logistics industry.

Salary and Benefits

  • Compensation: $1.5k-$2.5k/Month (approx. $24k/Year)
  • Benefits: A competitive compensation package is offered.
  • Flexible contract/gig opportunity in Chicago.

Day-to-Day

  • Apply your your professional skills skills at our Chicago location.

Build the Route Before the Sun Comes Up

Every morning, thousands of UPS drivers jump into perfectly loaded trucks, turn the key, and hit the road. That seamless execution is only possible because of the UPS Preload Package Handler. Operating during the very early morning hours (typically 3:00 AM to 8:00 AM), you are the architect of the delivery route. You will stand inside the back of the brown package cars, catching packages off a high-speed conveyor belt and loading them sequentially based on the driver's route map. If you want a fast-paced, intensely physical part-time job that provides incredible union benefits and frees up your entire day, this is the most critical warehouse role at UPS.

Preload Operations

  • High-Speed Package Sorting: Read alphanumeric routing codes on packages flying down the conveyor belt. You must quickly identify which packages belong to the 3 or 4 trucks you are assigned to load.
  • Sequential Truck Loading: This is a game of high-stakes Tetris. You must physically load the packages onto the specific interior shelves of the package car in the exact order the driver will deliver them, ensuring the heaviest boxes are safely secured on the floor.
  • Extreme Physical Conditioning: Skip the gym forever. You will be continuously twisting, bending, reaching, and lifting packages weighing up to 70 pounds for 4 to 5 hours straight in a fast-paced, loud, industrial environment.
  • Quality Control: Identify leaking, crushed, or mislabeled packages and pull them off the line for the problem-solve team before they are loaded onto the delivery truck.

The Part-Time Union Advantage

The UPS Preload position is legendary for its benefits. Even as a part-time employee, after a brief waiting period, you receive the same zero-premium, top-tier medical, dental, and vision insurance as full-time drivers. You are protected by the Teamsters union, receive regular wage increases, and get access to the "Earn and Learn" program, which provides massive tuition assistance for college students. Most importantly, Preload is the primary waiting list to become a highly-paid UPS Delivery Driver.

Requirements

Must be at least 18 years old. No driving license is required for this warehouse role. You must possess extreme physical stamina and athletic endurance to handle continuous heavy lifting up to 70 lbs. You must have the discipline to wake up and work extremely early morning hours (e.g., 3:00 AM starts). A reliable work ethic and ability to pass a background check are mandatory.

Warehouse and Parts Procurement Lead

Location: West Chicago, IL
Job Type: Full-Time

About Us

Chris Heating & Cooling is a third-generation, family-owned HVAC company dedicated to providing exceptional heating, cooling, and indoor air quality solutions. We pride ourselves on delivering outstanding customer service while fostering a positive, team-oriented work environment.

We're looking for a proactive and organized Warehouse and Parts Procurement Lead to oversee our warehouse operations, inventory management, and HVAC parts procurement. This is a hands-on leadership role responsible for ensuring our technicians and installers have the equipment, materials, and replacement parts they need to deliver an exceptional customer experience.

If you're someone who enjoys taking ownership, improving processes, building vendor relationships, and keeping operations running smoothly, we'd love to hear from you.

Responsibilities

  • Lead all warehouse operations, including receiving, inventory organization, shipping, material staging, and overall warehouse maintenance.
  • Procure HVAC equipment, replacement parts, tools, materials, and supplies from manufacturers and distributors.
  • Create, manage, and track purchase orders while ensuring pricing, quantities, and delivery dates are accurate.
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with HVAC suppliers and distributors while negotiating competitive pricing and monitoring vendor performance.
  • Research part availability, substitutions, lead times, and backorders to minimize technician downtime.
  • Monitor inventory levels and purchasing trends to ensure technicians and installers have the materials they need while minimizing excess inventory.
  • Track inventory turnover and identify slow-moving or obsolete inventory.
  • Receive, inspect, verify, and organize incoming shipments for accuracy and quality.
  • Pick, stage, and prepare equipment and materials for daily service and installation jobs.
  • Assist in maintaining truck stock inventory for field technicians.
  • Perform cycle counts, annual physical inventories, and reconcile inventory discrepancies.
  • Coordinate warranty claims, vendor credits, returns, damaged shipments, and core returns.
  • Maintain accurate inventory, purchasing, and receiving records using ServiceTitan and other company software.
  • Collaborate with dispatch, service managers, install managers, and technicians to forecast inventory needs and ensure parts are available for scheduled jobs.
  • Follow up with customers regarding recommended HVAC accessories, indoor air quality products, thermostats, filters, surge protectors, humidifiers, and other system enhancements that were previously quoted but not purchased.
  • Answer customer questions regarding accessories and coordinate installation scheduling when purchases are made.
  • Drive company vehicles to pick up HVAC parts, equipment, and materials from local suppliers and deliver inventory to technicians and job sites as needed.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe warehouse while promoting efficient workflows.
  • Recommend and implement improvements that increase inventory accuracy, purchasing efficiency, warehouse organization, and technician productivity.

  • Working knowledge of HVAC equipment, replacement parts, tools, installation materials, and indoor air quality products.

  • Experience creating and managing purchase orders.
  • Proficiency with inventory management software, ERP systems, or ServiceTitan is preferred.
  • Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Outlook and Excel.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, and customer service skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with technicians, office staff, vendors, and customers.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and safely operate warehouse equipment.
  • Forklift certification is a plus.
  • Valid driver's license with a clean driving record is required.
  • Must be comfortable driving company vehicles to pick up and deliver HVAC parts and equipment throughout the Chicagoland area.

jobs.description:
Testa Produce traces its roots back to 1912 when Dominick Testa started delivering produce to customers in Chicago. The company is now a member of the FreshEdge family of companies and run by Peter Testa, Dominick’s grandson. We offer a complete line of products to foodservice operators throughout Northern & Central Illinois, Southern Wisconsin and Northwest Indiana. While Testa Produce is known for its fresh fruits and vegetables as well as availability of special produce items, it also offers dry goods, frozen items and refrigerated meats and dairy items. Testa operates primarily out of its LEED platinum foodservice facility in the Back of the Yards neighborhood in Chicago but maintains a cross-dock facility in Milwaukee to service its Wisconsin customers. Testa Produce operates a fleet of roughly 55 refrigerated trucks and tractor-trailers all powered by Compressed Natural Gas. As our tagline says we are “Green by nature but Greener by Choice.


The Testa family is supported by an amazing team of transportation, warehouse, sales and administrative employees. We focus on meeting and exceeding our customers’ needs every day through hard work, creative thinking, use of technology and practical experience in the Produce/Distribution industry. We seek candidates that are looking to work in a team environment and are willing to become a contributing member of a family run business.


Job Summary


Pickers pick customer orders and stage pallets of product.


Duties and Responsibilities

  • Pick and stage orders on the Shipping Dock.
  • Check to correct quantity and quality on all product picked for ship out.

jobs.title: Manager, Warehouse
jobs.description:
Company Overview:
Hospeco Brand Group is the hub for a strategic collection of manufacturing and sales companies that lead the way in multiple categories — from personal care and protection to textiles, from cleaning products to contamination control — to empower its distributor partners into the future. Their cohesive approach promotes operational efficiency and fuels innovation, while equipping its varied businesses to tackle the toughest challenges across industrial and manufacturing, healthcare and life sciences, food service, hospitality, transportation, and many other dynamic market segments. Hospeco Brand Group’s rapid growth, both organic and via acquisition, is powered by its team of driven, innovative problem-solvers and a culture of integrity and respect.
Position Summary:
The Manager, Warehouse is responsible for leading all warehouse operations within a chemical mixing and distribution facility, ensuring the safe, compliant, and efficient handling of raw materials and finished goods. This role oversees inventory control, shipping and receiving, and team leadership while maintaining strict adherence to OSHA, EPA, and DOT regulations. The ideal candidate brings strong operational leadership experience in a regulated environment and a commitment to safety, accuracy, and continuous improvement.
Essential Functions and Responsibilities:
  • Oversee daily warehouse operations including receiving, storage, inventory control, picking, packing, and shipping of chemical products.
  • Ensure efficient workflow and optimal space utilization within the warehouse.
  • Partner with production and supply chain teams to align material availability with mixing and distribution schedules.
  • Enforce all safety protocols related to handling hazardous materials, including proper labeling, storage, and transport.
  • Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, DOT, and other applicable regulatory standards.
  • Lead safety training programs and maintain SDS documentation and hazard communication standards.
  • Conduct routine audits and inspections to maintain a safe working environment.
  • Maintain accurate inventory levels through cycle counts, reconciliations, and system updates.
  • Minimize product loss, damage, or contamination through proper handling and storage practices.
  • Utilize ERP/WMS systems to track and manage inventory movements.
  • Supervise, coach, and develop warehouse staff, including leads, forklift operators, and material handlers.
  • Manage staffing levels, scheduling, and performance evaluations.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, safety, and continuous improvement.
  • Coordinate inbound and outbound shipments, ensuring proper documentation for hazardous materials.
  • Work with carriers and logistics partners to ensure timely and cost-effective deliveries.
  • Ensure compliance with DOT shipping requirements, including proper packaging and labeling.
  • Identify and implement process improvements to increase efficiency, reduce costs, and improve service levels.
  • Track and report on KPIs such as order accuracy, on-time shipping, inventory accuracy, and safety metrics.
Qualifications:
  • 5–8+ years of warehouse or distribution experience, preferably in chemical, manufacturing, or regulated environments.
  • 2–4+ years of leadership or supervisory experience.
  • Strong knowledge of OSHA, EPA, and DOT regulations, including hazardous material handling.
  • Experience with ERP and/or Warehouse Management Systems (WMS).
  • Forklift certification (or ability to obtain).
  • Demonstrated ability to lead teams in a fast-paced, safety-critical environment.
  • Experience in a chemical mixing or blending environment.
  • Hazmat certification (e.g., DOT/IATA training).
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement experience.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Work Environment & Physical Requirements
  • Ability to work in a warehouse environment with exposure to chemicals, varying temperatures, and industrial equipment.
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs and operate material handling equipment.
  • Use of required PPE including gloves, goggles, and protective clothing.
Based on individual states’ employment laws, the salary range for this position is $80,000 - $85,000. Compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each candidate, including experience and location.

Ball Horticultural Company is seeking a detail-oriented and customer-focused candidate to join our Seed Processing Center as a Distribution Seed Handler. Ball is the world's largest breeder, producer, and distributor of flower seed, providing outstanding products, best-in-class customer service, and reliable supply to professional growers around the globe. In this role, you will support the accurate distribution of seed by packaging, verifying, storing, and maintaining inventory while ensuring quality standards, inventory accuracy, and timely order fulfillment.

jobs.title: Warehouse Operations Manager
jobs.description:
About CookUnity:

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry's best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul.

Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world.

If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you've found the right job posting.

The Role

As a Warehouse Operations Manager, you'll be responsible for managing the internal supply chain functions of our Facility.

You will play a vital role in ensuring the day-to-day success of the operation across all functions of the day-to-day business at CookUnity. You'll be a team leader, driving efficiency, accuracy, and a positive workplace culture across a team of hardworking warehouse Supervisors and Associates

This is an excellent opportunity for an individual who wants to take ownership inventory accuracy and excellent customer service to internal stakeholders.

Responsibilities

  • Manage accuracy and compliance of the ingredient and packaging receiving practices to ensure financial accuracy and operational efficiency.
  • Review site layouts to develop optimal storage and handling of ingredients and packaging
  • Focus on the "Distribution Model" deployment across all categories (Protein, Produce, Dairy, Dry Goods and Packaging) and Marketplaces
  • Develop and ensure ongoing compliance with process for checking incoming shipments versus invoices and order sheets.
  • Train and develop team members to ensure that they have the skills and resources required to successfully manage and handle all operational needs.
  • Focus on continuous improvement across core functions including but not limited to: receiving, inventory counting, purchasing, quality assurance, ingredient distribution and food safety compliance (HACCP).
  • Create and establish a food safety MOVEMENT! Implementing and complying with best in class handling, receiving and distribution practices by collaborating with our Food Safety Team.
  • Continuous oversight of inventory to ensure optimal levels of product
  • Aid in development and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to help ensure Marketplace functions are operating at highest efficiency levels
  • Maintain excellent relationships with our chef partners and work hand in hand with other departments across the CookUnity organization.
  • Understanding of Profit and Loss (P&L) statements, variance reports and KPI metrics
  • Oversight of scheduling for the Marketplace team, according to labor budget.
  • Any other marketplace tasks based on business needs.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in a similar role, managing receiving, shipping, inventory and/or warehousing functions in a manufacturing or wholesale distribution facility (food industry preferred).
  • Minimum of 3 years of people management experience
  • Strong understanding of HACCP and OSHA guidelines
  • Experience in food procurement and extensive food knowledge
  • Experience in inventory management
  • Expert understanding of supply chain or inventory control software (ERP, MRP, WMS platforms such as SAP, NetSuite, Infor, etc.)
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented
  • Understanding of food safety and quality standards
  • Ability to promote professional growth and development of the entire Marketplace team.
  • Ability to communicate and understand Spanish is preferred.
  • Ability to travel 5-10% as needed to support other locations

Benefits

  • Health Insurance coverage
    • PTO policy and paid sick days
  • We grow, you grow: Stock Options Plan granted on Day 1.
  • Eligible for bi-annual performance bonus
  • Family leave fully paid
  • Compassionate Leave: 3-5 days each time the need arises
  • A generous amount of CookUnity credits to enjoy our amazing meals, added to your account, monthly
  • ‍️ Wellness perks: access to fitness subsidies to build a healthy lifestyle
    • ‍
  • Personalized Spanish coach
  • Awesome opportunity to join a company that is looking to change how we eat and how chefs work!

  • ️ 5- year Sabbatical: After 5 years with CookUnity, you get a 4-week paid sabbatical

#ENG1P

If you're interested in this role, please submit your application, and if we think you might be a fit, we'll get in touch with you. Thank you for your time!


CookUnity is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are dedicated to creating a community of inclusion and an environment free from discrimination or harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, citizenship status, protected veteran status, genetic information, or physical or mental disability.

A quick note for all candidates
We've recently seen an increase in recruitment scams across the industry, and we want to make sure you (and your data) stay safe while applying to CookUnity. We also want you to know that we take this seriously — sometimes, as part of our process, we may ask for a brief "proof of humanity" to confirm that we're connecting with a real person, not an impersonator. Here are a few tips to help you protect yourself and know what to expect from us:

  • Apply only through our official channels. All open roles are listed on our official careers page: careers.cookunity.com
  • Our recruiters are real people — and easy to verify. You can always find them on LinkedIn with verified profiles. If you're unsure, feel free to reach out to us on our official LinkedIn Company Page.
  • We only communicate through official CookUnity channels. That means emails ending in @cookunity.com and interviews held through official company platforms (Google Meet or Zoom) — never WhatsApp, Telegram, or SMS.
  • We'll never ask for payment or personal financial details. If anyone does, please don't share any information and let us know right away.

If something ever feels off or you're unsure about a message, we'd much rather you double-check with us. You can always contact us directly through any of our social media channels. We appreciate your interest in joining CookUnity — and we care about keeping your experience (and safety) as genuine as possible.

What started as a small antique store in 1977 has become a nationally recognized neighborhood sandwich shop with over 400 locations across the United States. But toasty sandwiches are only as good as the people behind them. And yeah, we've got the best. Ready to join our growing Potbelly Nation?

No two days in our warehouse look the same — and that’s exactly how we like it.


One day you might be gathering and staging materials for a brand-new Potbelly shop getting ready to open. The next, you could be packaging individual items for shipping to existing shops, cleaning and organizing the warehouse, or helping prep millwork and materials for finishing.


If you’re mechanically minded, enjoy working with your hands, and tackling unique projects, you’ll fit right in. Our warehouse team keeps things moving behind the scenes and plays a huge role in helping our shops succeed.


This isn’t a sit-at-a-desk-all-day kind of job. It’s hands-on, fast-paced, physical work where teamwork, organization, and problem-solving matter. If you like variety, staying busy, and seeing the direct impact of your work, you’ll probably love it here.

  • Pulls and distributes materials, artifacts, or other stock items to fill orders.

  • Receives goods and enters all items into inventory.

  • Must be able to lift up to 75 pounds frequently.
  • Must be able to communicate through telephone, e-mail and in-person communications.

EXPERIENCE, EDUCATION AND BEHAVIORS

  • Must process orders and move boxes of files, books, binders, backup tapes, and other materials.

  • The work is very physical, requiring manual lifting, carrying, and moving/arranging boxes while standing, stooping, crawling, kneeling, and twisting.
  • Must be able to lift and carry boxes ranging in weight from 10-100lbs on a regular basis, without assistance.
  • Must be able to load and safely operate hand trucks and pallet jacks while walking on uneven and concrete surfaces.

jobs.title: Material Handler Night Shift (7pm-7am)
jobs.description:
Material Handler Night Shift (7pm-7am)

Winpak Portion Packaging is seeking a Material Handler to join the Production Dept based out of our Sauk Village and/or Chicago Heights facilities. In this role you will safely and efficiently service the production lines by supplying or removing materials, in a timely manner, to ensure no downtime is incurred and inventory remains accurate.

Join our Production Department at our Sauk Village facility as a Material Handler. In this role, you will play a key part in supporting production operations by safely and efficiently supplying materials to the production lines and removing finished or excess materials. Your attention to accuracy and timeliness will help ensure continuous production with minimal downtime and maintain precise inventory control. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who thrives in a fast-paced manufacturing environment and is committed to safety, teamwork, and operational excellence.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Verify and understand material requirements for assigned jobs.
  • Obtain necessary materials from the warehouse or request them from the remote warehouse as needed.
  • Prepare materials for production (e.g., cleaning, unwrapping, labeling).
  • Safely and promptly deliver materials to machines, ensuring continuous operation and minimizing downtime.
  • Monitor machines and replenish materials as needed to support uninterrupted production.
  • Accurately document material inspections, usage, and assignments in a clear and legible manner.
  • Maintain up-to-date and accurate inventory row tags.
  • Retrieve carts, unused or rejected materials, and other necessary items efficiently.
  • Properly wrap, weigh, label, and store any unused or rejected materials.
  • Keep the work area clean, organized, and safe throughout the shift.
  • Maintain a valid forklift operator certification and operate forklifts safely and efficiently.
  • Complete and document forklift inspections at the start of each shift.
  • Immediately report any safety, material, machine, tooling, quality, or process issues to a supervisor.
  • Manage time effectively to reduce downtime, optimize production, and complete cleaning, inspections, and documentation within the work shift.
  • Comply with all safety policies, procedures, and use of personal protective equipment.
  • Adhere to all personal hygiene and dress code requirements, including appropriate hair coverings.
  • Report any food packaging safety concerns directly to plant management.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.
  • In the event of absence, responsibilities will be delegated to an alternate qualified Material Handler.

Required Qualifications:

  • Follow Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP): Adhere to all company GMP policies to ensure the safe handling and integrity of food packaging materials.
  • Maintain Sanitation Standards: Support and follow sanitation procedures to uphold cleanliness and reduce contamination risks in all work areas.
  • Quality Assurance Support: Handle and inspect materials in a way that supports the plant\'s quality objectives, preventing mix-ups, contamination, or damage.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Forklift experience.
  • Basic math skills.
  • Basic computer skills.
    • Lifting/carrying up to 50 lbs regularly.
    • Walking/standing approximately 12 hours per day

Additional Information:

  • The Material Handler position is 100% onsite, working on the production floor.
  • 12-Hour COP Shift Rotation:
  • Week 1 - Monday, Tuesday, Friday & Saturday
  • Week 2 - Sunday, Wednesday & Thursday

Compensation range:

The compensation range is $18.20- 25.35 and is provided as a general guideline only. Pay will be determined based on the candidate\'s experience and expertise and is subject to vary.
